title: Nanoporous polymer-derived activated carbon for hydrogen adsorption and electrochemical energy storage
material_description: PDAC | polyaniline (PANi)-derived activated carbon powder: PANi hydrogel (aniline, phytic acid, ammonium persulfate) freeze-dried to an aerogel, carbonized under N2 and activated with KOH (synthesized and provided by Z. Bao and co-workers, Stanford); degassed before measurement
activation_method: KOH chemical activation after carbonization of the PANi aerogel under N2
source_location: main p.6, Fig. 3a, series PDAC @ 77 K, filled circles (adsorption), digitized marker 1
notes: archive: fig3a_PDAC_77K_adsorption.json (point 1); pressure digitized as 13.0781 mbar and converted to bar; wt% convention W2 per Table 3 footnote (C_g = m_gas/(m_gas + m_solid)). Low-pressure H2 isotherm, Quantachrome Autosorb-1-MP manometric analyzer with Gifford-McMahon cryocooler ('using the same system' as the Ar measurements); degassing (~50 mg, 10^-6 mbar = 1e-4 Pa, 250 C, 12 h) and He void-volume calculation are stated in the Ar paragraph for this system and applied here. isotherm_point_count 57 is a lower bound: 32 separable filled markers, >=6 overlapping filled markers below ~13 mbar, >=3 overlapping filled markers at ~0.97-1.01 bar, 16 open markers (see log.md). Characterization (Table 1, Ar 87 K, QSDFT slit kernel): surface area is the QSDFT S_DFT (no BET area reported; probe Ar at 87 K, not N2/77 K); S_DFT(MP) <2 nm = micropore area; V_DFT (pores <36 nm) = total pore volume; V_DFT(MP) = micropore volume; average_pore_diameter = volume-weighted median d50 0.92 nm (d25-d75 0.72-1.30 nm). SAXS: S_SAXS 2360 m2/g, t 0.54 nm, l_carbon 0.79 nm, l_pore 1.69 nm. Skeletal density ~2.15 g/cm3 (He pycnometry); packing density = poured bulk density ~0.45 g/cm3 (2 mL container). Raman La ~5.1 nm. N content 0.5-2.3 wt% (XPS) is reported only for similar PANi-derived carbons in ref. [29], not measured here, so no dopant coded.
basis_evidence: Named 'excess' without definition: Table 3 title 'Summary of the excess gravimetric and volumetric H2 storage capacities'; Fig. 3 caption '(c) high-pressure (up to 80 bar) excess H2 adsorption (closed symbols)'; abstract 'excess gravimetric H2 uptake of ~5.5 wt% at 77 K'
free_volume_calibration: He (99.999%) void-volume calculation on the Autosorb-1-MP; temperature not stated
